title: Two-way lookup with VLOOKUP and MATCH

screens.prompt: In C6, return the units for the product in A6 and the quarter in B6, using VLOOKUP and letting MATCH find the column.

hints.syntax: =VLOOKUP(A6,A1:C5,MATCH(B6,A1:C1,0),FALSE) — MATCH turns the quarter into the column number.
hints.func-vlookup: VLOOKUP is the half that fetches the number. It needs the product, the table, and the column number MATCH hands it.
hints.func-match: MATCH needs three arguments: the quarter, the header row A1:C1, and 0. Given two it reads nothing and reports a missing argument.
hints.require-ref: Point MATCH at B6. Typing "Q2" into the formula works until the cell changes, which is the one thing this drill is about.
hints.match-exact: MATCH's third argument must be 0 or FALSE. Anything else is an approximate match, which assumes the header is sorted.
hints.value: MATCH returns a position inside the range you gave it, and VLOOKUP counts columns from the first column of its table. Start both at the Product column and the positions line up.
hints.error: Read the code: #N/A means the product or the quarter matched nothing, #REF! means the column number reached past the last column, and #VALUE! means text landed where a number or a condition belongs.
hints.match-type: Write FALSE as VLOOKUP's fourth argument. TRUE is an approximate match, so VLOOKUP stops wherever it likes and answers with another row.

accept: =VLOOKUP( A6 , A1:C5 , MATCH( B6 , A1:C1 , 0 ) , FALSE )

reject.why: the right answer with the wrong function
the column number typed in, which breaks when a quarter is inserted
MATCH without the 0, so it is a two-argument call
the quarter typed into the formula instead of read from B6
approximate MATCH on an unsorted header, which can land on any column
MATCH counted from B, so its 2 came out as Q1
approximate VLOOKUP, which stops on the last row it saw
#VALUE!: the column number became the text 3x
the word no where TRUE or FALSE belongs, so the match mode is unreadable

docs.explain: MATCH reads the header A1:C1 for the quarter in B6 and returns 3, because Q2 is the third column of the table. VLOOKUP then finds Widget on row 3 of A1:C5 and takes that row's 3rd value: 110. No digit in the formula names a column, so changing B6 to Q1 returns 90 without editing the formula. The two ranges have to start on the same column for this to work: MATCH counts inside the range it was given, and VLOOKUP counts from the first column of its table, so a MATCH over B1:C1 returns 2 and lands on Q1.

errors.text: MATCH could not find the quarter in the header, or VLOOKUP could not find the product in the first column.
A text value reached an argument that needs a number, usually the MATCH position joined to characters, so VLOOKUP was handed a column number it cannot count with.
The column number from MATCH is wider than the table, which happens when MATCH reads a header that starts before the table does.

docs.atWork: Units by product and quarter, headcount by team and month, price by SKU and currency: any grid where the column you need is itself a lookup.
docs.outcome: Return one cell of a grid from a row key and a column key, without counting columns.
